segments.title: Chương 190
segments.content:
Chapter 193: Overloaded Servers

Xiang Weijie's high school grades were not ideal, so now he could only attend a junior college.

He was even playing games the day before the Gaokao. Anyway, his family wasn't short on money, and no one cared about him.

His parents initially sold clothes at a street stall, then started a family garment workshop, specializing in copying popular styles from Hong Kong and Taiwan. As business boomed, more than twenty families in the village followed suit.

His parents seized the opportunity to form a company, centrally purchasing raw materials like fabric and buttons to sell to the villagers for clothing production. They would then buy the finished garments from the villagers and wholesale them as counterfeit brand-name products.

The business grew larger and larger, and soon, villages for miles around joined in.

There were also those who didn't follow his parents' lead; there were three similar companies in the entire town.

His parents continued to upgrade, wholesaling counterfeit brands while also creating their own. His father was perennially away expanding sales channels, while his mother stayed in their hometown to manage production.

Soon, his father had an affair while he was away. He not only had a mistress but also an illegitimate son.

The couple fought a few times but ended up maintaining the status quo. His mother later got herself a boy toy, even bringing him home occasionally and making Xiang Weijie call him Uncle…

Xiang Weijie had boarded at school since junior high, and in high school, he completely let himself go, just wasting his days away playing games.

When it came time to choose his college, despite his family being on the southeast coast, he directly applied to a junior college in the central Sichuan region. The farther from home, the better!

"Fucking hell, I'll beat that son of a bitch to death next time!"

"Beat my ass, you'll get expelled if you fight again."

"Why should I be expelled? He stole my girlfriend! If anyone's getting expelled, it should be him!"

Two of his roommates returned to the dorm, cursing.

Xiang Weijie turned his head to see his roommates, Li Jun and Pan Qiang, with torn clothes and bruised faces.

"Did you guys get into a fight?" Xiang Weijie asked.

Pan Qiang said, "Someone stole Li Jun's girlfriend. A few of us went to demand an explanation and got into a fight with the other guys."

Li Jun was utterly dejected, cursing, "Bitch! Using my money and wearing the clothes I bought all the time, yet she was hooking up with another guy behind my back. If the dean's office staff hadn't shown up, I definitely would've beaten that bastard and bitch to death today!"

Xiang Weijie smiled and offered a casual word of comfort, "Kill him, I'll support you."

He actually despised Li Jun, so he was secretly gloating.

Pan Qiang changed out of his ripped clothes and sat down next to Xiang Weijie. "What are you doing?"

"Waiting for a game server to launch," Xiang Weijie said.

"Playing a private server again?" Pan Qiang asked.

Xiang Weijie said, "'Sovereignty of the World' is launching tonight. I've already downloaded the game."

"Is that the one you're always hyping up?" Pan Qiang asked.

Xiang Weijie raised his voice, once again evangelizing to his roommates, "I'm really not just hyping it. The boss of this game is super awesome. He used to make private servers. To make a legitimate game, he sold his internet cafe and car. When the money ran out, he was even preparing to sell his house, but he finally got an investment from a big company."

Li Jun said impatiently, "You've said that countless times, I can recite it by heart. My buddy's company invested in it, right? ByteDance!"

"Your buddy's company invested, and you're still not playing?" Xiang Weijie asked.

"What's the point of playing games? I'd rather play basketball," Li Jun said.

Li Jun didn't go online much and never played video games, but he had bought the second computer in the dorm.

Because Xiang Weijie had one, Li Jun had to have one too, or else he would feel like he was losing face.

Li Jun glanced around the dorm. "Where are the others?"

"Li Yuan took Zhang Peng and Du Ruifeng to get computers," Xiang Weijie said. "Li Yuan's uncle owns a computer shop. You can get a used one for 3000 yuan."

Pan Qiang was curious. "Where did Zhang Peng get the money? That son of a bitch still owes me a few dozen yuan."

Xiang Weijie laughed. "He hasn't paid this year's tuition yet."

"He used his tuition money to buy a computer?"

"Yeah."

"Awesome!"

As they were talking, two roommates returned triumphantly, each carrying a computer tower.

After putting down the towers, they ran out again and soon returned with monitors, then ran out once more. It turned out another roommate had been guarding the things downstairs the whole time.

Soon, the number of computers in the dorm went from two to five.

Zhang Peng even took out a router. "We'll use the campus network for now. We can get a broadband connection another day."

The campus network required you to add credit first, then log in with an account and password. The rate was 30 cents per hour. But it would disconnect at 11 PM, which was very frustrating for students who wanted to stay up late online.

Xiang Weijie often stayed out all night. Even though he had his own computer, he would go to an internet cafe to play through the night.

"Hey, hurry up and download the game. Come play 'Sovereignty of the World' with me," Xiang Weijie urged.

"I bought a computer to play 'World of Warcraft'."

"Zhang Peng, 'World of Warcraft' requires you to buy game time cards. 'Sovereignty of the World' is free!"

"Really free?"

"I'd be an idiot to lie to you."

"I'll play it then."

"Damn it, Zhang Peng, you promised to play 'Warcraft' with me!"

"I don't have any money. I used my tuition to buy the computer."

"Let's try it first. If it's no good, we can play 'Warcraft'."

After some back and forth, everyone downloaded "Sovereignty of the World."

Even Pan Qiang, who didn't have a computer, used Li Jun's to download the game.

Seeing them all about to play games, Li Jun found himself with nothing to do and suddenly felt isolated.

He wanted to pull Pan Qiang away from the computer, but Pan Qiang had just helped him in a fight today.

"Damn, you guys haven't downloaded it yet? The server is about to launch!"

"Bro, the campus network is slow."

At 8 PM, the server launched on time.

"Sovereignty of the World" was purely original. The general framework came from Chen Guiliang, and the details were filled in by Tao Chenggang and his team.

Tao Chenggang also made modifications to the world-building provided by Chen Guiliang.

Qi, Chu, Yan, Han, Zhao, Wei, Qin… seven warring states.

When players entered the game, they had to choose their state.

To prevent a large disparity in the number of players between states, once a state reached its population cap, it could no longer be chosen.

If a state's daily active user count was too low, the state's king would issue a "Recruitment Order," encouraging players from other states to immigrate, offering rewards for completing immigration quests.

Each state had five maps: Royal City, Wilderness, Major Town, Borderlands, and Novice Village.

Of course, the specific names were different. For example, the Royal City of Qin was called Xianyang.

The other roommates were still downloading the game, gathered behind Xiang Weijie. Li Jun found it boring and went to take a shower.

"Pick Qin, it's the most badass!"

"Chu. I like Chu the most."

"How come there's a Han state?"

"Damn it, even if I'm only in a junior college, I know Han is part of China!"

Xiang Weijie ultimately chose Qin and was born in a novice village called "Wei River Village."

"Quick, go to the NPC with the exclamation mark to get a quest," advised Li Yuan, who was familiar with "World of Warcraft."

"I know."

Xiang Weijie didn't act immediately. Instead, he stood in the novice village and typed: Any brothers from 17173 here?

Instantly, a bunch of people in the novice village responded.

They were all from the "Sovereignty of the World" section on 17173.

Xiang Weijie chatted as he went to accept a quest.

The village chief of the novice village told him that a large number of wild boars had appeared in the village and were ruining the crops, hoping he could clear out the pests.

Opening the quest interface, Xiang Weijie found the relevant quest and discovered there was an auto-pathing function.

Shi Yuzhu was also playing "Sovereignty of the World" at this moment.

Although he didn't think much of the game, he still decided to try it out.

Know yourself and know your enemy, and you will never be defeated.

As he played, Shi Yuzhu's brows furrowed.

This thing's gameplay is so similar to my "Zhengtu"!

Mine has ten states, theirs has seven.

But the polish on this game was clearly higher than "Zhengtu."

"Zhengtu," which was set for closed beta next month, was a very rough, half-finished game. It had no auto-pathing function, the UI was not aesthetically pleasing, information displays were unclear, and the skill bar was inconvenient to switch…

Moreover, "Zhengtu" had elements from Legend like killing chickens. "Sovereignty of the World" felt less out of place, with only humanoid monsters like bandits and animal monsters like wild boars and wolves.

The early version of "Zhengtu" had no dungeons; all resources had to be fought for. Shi Yuzhu believed this could enhance player activity and competition.

But in "Sovereignty of the World," players could run small dungeons upon reaching level 15.

Shi Yuzhu took a hard drag from his cigarette, walked out of his office, and said, "Assign three people to play 'Sovereignty of the World.' See what content is worth borrowing!"

Falling behind for a moment was no big deal; Shi Yuzhu wasn't worried.

Tao Chenggang's Blazing Technology was just a small company with a truly limited budget for publicity and promotion. But he, Boss Shi, had already prepared over a hundred million yuan to throw at it!

He had even spent 20 million on initial R&D, paying every developer the highest salary in the entire industry. Furthermore, anyone who proposed an excellent idea that was adopted was directly rewarded with company stock options.

"Sovereignty of the World" being ahead for a little while meant nothing.

At 10:30 PM, in the school dormitory.

All five of them were in the game.

His four roommates were shouting and yelling, asking Xiang Weijie to lead them through quests to level up.

Xiang Weijie said, "Lead my ass, I'm going to the internet cafe. Damn it, we're getting broadband tomorrow. I can't pull an all-nighter on the campus network!"

Li Jun, having returned from his shower, saw them playing with such enthusiasm and was now eager to try. "Xiang Weijie, let me use your computer and campus network account. I'll pay you back for the internet fee."

"Go ahead, then." Xiang Weijie packed his things and left.

Li Jun had never played an online game before. Upon entering the game, it was as if a new world's gate had opened.

He used to think his roommates were idiots for mindlessly killing monsters. Now that he was doing it himself, he found it incredibly interesting.

"Fuck, the internet's disconnected!"

At 11 PM, the campus network went down.

Li Jun was right in the middle of the fun, itching to continue. He said, "Let's go, to the internet cafe together."

"No need, we can play tomorrow after we get broadband."

"I'm going."

"I'll go with you."

After some dithering, the entire dorm ended up going to the internet cafe.

Today was Saturday, and the dormitory building didn't lock its doors until 11:30 PM, so they didn't have to climb out through the drainpipes.

As for Xiang Weijie, who had arrived at the internet cafe earliest, he booted up a computer, found that "Sovereignty of the World" wasn't installed, and called the attendant over. "You're missing some games here."

"What game?"

"'Sovereignty of the World.'"

"Never heard of it."

"It's a super awesome game. Closed beta started today."

The attendant was busy playing "World of Warcraft" and told him to download it himself.

In the middle of the night, Xiang Weijie suddenly shot to his feet and roared, "Fuck, that asshole party leader ninja'd the purple gear!"

Many people nearby playing Warcraft came over to see what was going on, only to find it wasn't "World of Warcraft."

"Bro, what game is this? How come it has dungeons like Warcraft?"

"'Sovereignty of the World.' It's free-to-play, no game time cards."

"The graphics are total crap compared to Warcraft."

"No kidding, can they be compared? Let me tell you, the boss of this game made it for his dream. He sold his internet cafe, car, and house. If we don't support him, he'll definitely be bankrupt."

"For real?"

"If you don't believe me, go read the posts on 17173. They've been documenting it for over a year, from founding the company to the closed beta. Even the game's name was decided by a user poll. I even submitted a name called 'Samurai Warriors' and got over 600 votes, but it wasn't chosen in the end. Wanna try a couple rounds?"

"I wanna play Warcraft."

"Just think of it as supporting a domestic game, helping the boss fulfill his dream."

"Forget it."

Another person playing Crazy Arcade suddenly asked, "Is it really a free game?"

"It is."

"I'll give it a try then."

In the dead of night.

Luo Xiaoping, one of the founders and the technical lead of Blazing Technology, said, "Last night's peak concurrent users were nearly 20,000. Both server groups were overloaded, and it was especially laggy around 9 o'clock. We'll have to open another server tomorrow."

A single server for "Sovereignty of the World" was designed for a capacity of 5,000 to 8,000 concurrent users. The actual peak could reach 10,000, but it would be so laggy you couldn't function.

A single server for "World of Warcraft" was designed for a capacity of 2,500 to 3,000 concurrent users. But the actual peak often exceeded 4,000.

This was because "World of Warcraft" used a seamless, large world map, which put a heavy load on the servers.

Tao Chenggang's immense pressure had eased slightly. He took a drag from his cigarette and said, "The player feedback on the official website and 17173 is pretty good. We'll see how many of the first batch of players stick around tomorrow."

"It's definitely going to be a hit!" Luo Xiaoping said with a smile.

Tao Chenggang said, "Pay attention to player feedback. Fix any bugs immediately. Also, post more announcements. Anyone found using cheats will have their account banned, no exceptions!"

Tao Chenggang felt the results were quite good, with nearly 20,000 concurrent users on the first day of closed beta.

But "Zhengtu" from another timeline was the truly incredible one, breaking 10,000 users in 10 minutes and 30,000 in 3 hours. Because only three servers were opened, players who couldn't get in angrily spammed the forums, cursing, "All you know is to burn money on advertising, why can't you open a few more servers?"

At noon the next day, "Sovereignty of the World" opened its third server.

That evening, all three servers were full to bursting, and the lag finally made players start complaining. But some players also voluntarily helped explain, "The boss doesn't have much money, he can't afford to rent more servers."

Tao Chenggang frowned deeply. "How can there be so many people?"

He went to the 17173 section to look for posts and soon found the reason.

"Haha, I've dragged all my dorm brothers into this pit!"

"I got the internet cafe attendant to install 'Sovereignty of the World' on every computer. Today, seven other people in the cafe were playing with me. They used to play 'Rexue Jianghu,' but now they've switched to 'Sovereignty of the World'."

Tao Chenggang's game had a hell of a lot of die-hard fans generating word-of-mouth promotion!

These loyal fans had even started helping promote the game before the closed beta had even launched.

At this time in mainland China, there were only about twenty or thirty online games worth mentioning.

On the second day of its closed beta, "Sovereignty of the World" reached 30,000 concurrent users, quickly attracting the attention of all game companies.

Because this game was too strange, it had exploded in numbers out of nowhere, without even having the money for promotion.

Recommending the author's new book: "I Attain Immortality Through the Imperial Examinations." You can guess the content from the title. Those interested can go check it out.

(End of this chapter)
